questions.question: When should a team add an advanced retrieval stage?
options: Whenever a larger model is available.
After a sliced evaluation identifies a repeatable retrieval failure the stage can address.
Before building a single-query baseline.
Whenever the context window is longer than the source document.
questions.explanation: Every extra stage adds work and failure modes. Add it for a named, measured gap such as missing multi-part evidence or vocabulary mismatch.

questions.question: Why can reciprocal rank fusion combine lexical and vector result lists without normalizing their raw scores?
options: It uses each document's rank position in each list instead of comparing score scales.
Lexical and vector scores always use the same range.
It asks the language model to rewrite every score.
It discards every document that appears in only one list.
questions.explanation: RRF sums reciprocal contributions derived from rank positions, so incompatible BM25 and vector score magnitudes do not need to be compared directly.

questions.question: With RRF constant 60, what contribution does a document receive when it is ranked second in one active list?
questions.explanation: The visible formula is 1 / (constant + rank), so second place contributes 1 / (60 + 2) = 1 / 62.

questions.question: What is the safety boundary for a HyDE hypothetical passage?
options: Treat it as the most authoritative source.
Use it to steer retrieval, but answer only from real, authorized corpus evidence.
Store it as a new policy document.
Cite it when no real document matches.
questions.explanation: HyDE's generated passage is a search representation and may contain false details. It must not become answer evidence.

questions.question: A hierarchical retriever selects the wrong parent section. What follows?
options: A reranker automatically searches every other section.
Relevant leaf passages below other parents can become unreachable.
The vector index repairs the document hierarchy.
Generation becomes grounded by default.
questions.explanation: Hierarchical retrieval narrows the search space through parent choices, so parent recall must be evaluated separately from leaf ranking.

questions.question: Which production trace best supports debugging an adaptive RAG request?
options: Only the final answer text.
The router decision, query variants, index version, ranked candidates, selected evidence, gate verdict, and any fallback.
Only the model's self-reported confidence.
The total token count without source identities.
questions.explanation: Adaptive retrieval introduces branching and retries. Replaying the request requires the chosen path, versions, evidence transitions, and release decision.
